name: MemoryBank

paper.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory

construction.unit: one dialogue exchange (user query + AI response) with its date; per-day event summary and personality analysis; global event summary and global user portrait
construction.kept_as: exchanges verbatim; summaries and portraits written by an LLM
construction.processing: every exchange appended to today's log; on request at login, an LLM summarises each day's events and the user's personality, then summarises all days into a global summary and portrait
construction.writer: gpt-3.5-turbo for all summaries in the code (summarize_memory.py), for every SiliconFriend variant

organization.structure: per-day log -> daily summaries -> global summary; daily personality -> global portrait
organization.stores: one JSON memory file per deployment (history, summary, personality, overall_history, overall_personality per user); FAISS index per user
organization.index: dense embeddings of each exchange and each daily event summary (MiniLM for English, Text2vec for Chinese)

management.operations: summaries regenerated on request; forgetting drops exchanges at random by an Ebbinghaus-style retention
management.forgetting: paper: retention R = e^(-t/S), S starts at 1 and +1 on each recall with t reset; code: optional path, off by default, formula e^(-t·S/5), forgotten exchanges deleted from the file

retrieval.candidates: FAISS dense search over exchanges and daily summaries
retrieval.selection: top-k by similarity (k = 2 by default in the ChatGLM/BELLE demo), adjacent same-day pieces merged up to 200 characters

use.context: retrieved memories with their dates, global user portrait and reply strategy, recent session turns (paper also lists the global event summary; the code never inserts it)

classify.note: The forgetting curve is the paper's management contribution, so management is 'evict', but the released code runs it only on an opt-in path whose module is missing. The hierarchy (day -> global summaries) matters little for retrieval, which is flat over exchanges and daily summaries.

stages.ingestion: Every user-AI exchange is appended verbatim to the user's log under today's date.
stages.construction: On request (at login in the demos) an LLM writes a daily event summary and a daily personality/emotion analysis for each unsummarised day, then a global event summary and a global personality portrait with a reply strategy.
stages.organization: Exchanges and daily summaries are embedded (MiniLM for English, Text2vec for Chinese) into a FAISS index, rebuilt whenever the user logs in.
stages.update: Paper: each memory has strength S (1 at first mention); recall adds 1 and resets elapsed time; memories fade by R = e^(-t/S). Code: when the optional path is enabled, each exchange is kept with probability e^(-t·S/5) at login and deleted otherwise.
stages.retrieval: The current user message is embedded and the top 2 pieces are retrieved (ChatGLM/BELLE demo default), grouped by date. The ChatGPT variant queries a LlamaIndex vector index over whole-day documents and gets an LLM-written answer back.
stages.answer: The meta prompt holds the retrieved memories and their dates, the global user portrait with the reply strategy, and the last 7 exchanges of the session.
stages.learning: No memory learning. Separately, the open-source SiliconFriend backbones (ChatGLM, BELLE) are LoRA-tuned on 38k psychological dialogues for empathy.

summary: Early long-term memory for LLM chat companions: a dated log of exchanges with LLM-written daily and global summaries and a user portrait, dense retrieval of past exchanges, and an Ebbinghaus-style forgetting rule where recalled memories get stronger.

sources.code_note: Last commit on main (2023-05-24), three days after arXiv v3. It holds the SiliconFriend demos (ChatGLM/BELLE CLI and web app, ChatGPT CLI), the memory code and the evaluation memories and probing questions, but no script that produces Table 2 (scores were given by human annotators).

headline: Memory is the verbatim log of exchanges plus LLM summaries; the reply model sees only 2 retrieved pieces, the user portrait and recent turns.
The global event summary is built but never enters the prompt in the released code: the templates have no slot for it.
The Ebbinghaus forgetting rule is off by default in the code, and where implemented a stronger memory decays faster (e^(-t·S/5)), the opposite of the paper.

answer_context.format: companion meta prompt: role and duties, 'the most relevant [memory] is: {related_memory_content} The date of this [memory] is {memo_dates}', 'refer to user {user_name}'s personality and the AI's response strategy: {personality}', then [|User|]/[|AI|] turns

answer_context.note: ChatGPT variant: the system prompt holds an answer that LlamaIndex's LLM wrote from the retrieved whole-day documents, not the documents themselves.

compression.what: answer context vs the stored history
compression.basis: Not reported. The paper gives no token counts; the evaluation store has 10 days and 49 exchanges per user in the repo files.

paper_vs_code.paper: R = e^(-t/S); S grows with recall so recalled memories last longer
paper_vs_code.code: math.exp(-t / 5*S) = e^(-t·S/5): larger S forgets faster; path is opt-in and its import target forget_memory_new is missing

paper_vs_code.paper: relevant memory, global user portrait and global event summary
paper_vs_code.code: history_summary is computed but no template has a {history_summary} slot
100 English and 100 Chinese questions in eval_data

open_questions: No no-memory or plain-retrieval baseline is reported, so Table 2 cannot show what MemoryBank adds over the backbone alone or over simple RAG.
The ChatGPT variant retrieves with LlamaIndex over whole days while ChatGLM/BELLE use FAISS over single exchanges, so retrieval accuracy differences mix retriever and backbone.

components.model: LlamaIndex GPTSimpleVectorIndex with gpt-3.5-turbo answer synthesis
ChatGLM-6B or BELLE-7B (LoRA on psychology data), or ChatGPT

discussion.takeaway: An early, simple recipe for companion memory: keep the dated chat log, summarise days and the user's personality with an LLM, retrieve a few past exchanges by embedding, and decay unused memories. Its evaluation is a small human-scored probe of three SiliconFriend variants without baselines.

claims.claim: MemoryBank lets LLMs recall past interactions and adapt to the user's personality.
It works with both open- and closed-source LLMs.
claims.evidence: Retrieval accuracy 0.763-0.856 for ChatGLM, BELLE and ChatGPT variants in English and Chinese. Table 2

claims.claim: The ChatGPT variant gives the best responses overall.
claims.evidence: English correctness 0.716, coherence 0.912, ranking 0.818 vs 0.438-0.479 correctness for ChatGLM/BELLE. Table 2

claims.claim: Psychology tuning gives more empathetic replies.
claims.evidence: Comparison with base ChatGLM on a real conversation. Fig. 2

limits: The memory updating model is exploratory and highly simplified; real forgetting depends on the person and the kind of information.
reading: The quantitative test has no baseline without memory or with plain retrieval, and only compares three variants of the paper's own system with human labels; the number of annotators is not stated.
The paper does not say whether the forgetting mechanism was on for the Table 2 runs; in the code it is off by default and cannot be switched on without a missing module.
Where forgetting is implemented, e^(-t·S/5) makes frequently recalled memories decay faster, the reverse of the paper's rule; daily summaries are never decayed.
The global event summary is computed but not placed in any prompt template.

ChatGLM/BELLE retrieve single exchanges from FAISS, while the ChatGPT variant retrieves whole-day documents through LlamaIndex and receives an LLM-written answer; its lower retrieval accuracy (0.763/0.711) comes from a different retriever, not only a different backbone.
The repository has 100 probing questions per language; the paper reports 97 per language.

abstract.text: MemoryBank adds long-term memory to LLM chatbots. It stores the dated conversation log, LLM-written daily and global event summaries, and an evolving portrait of the user's personality, and retrieves relevant past exchanges with a dense retriever. An update rule inspired by the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve lets memories fade with time and strengthen when recalled. The authors build SiliconFriend, a companion bot on ChatGPT, ChatGLM and BELLE (the latter two LoRA-tuned on psychological dialogues), and test memory recall with simulated 10-day conversations of 15 users and human-scored probing questions.
